topIssues.title: bug(op-reth): memory leak during op proof backfill using cli
topIssues.author: dhyaniarun1993
topIssues.body:
**Bug Description**
The op-proofs CLI's backfill leaks process-anonymous memory. Memory is never released for the lifetime of the process. jemalloc heap-profile diff (between two .heap files captured ~7 hours apart) pins the root cause to metrics-`util::storage::bucket::AtomicBucket::push`, called via histogram records inside `reth_trie::trie::StateRoot::calculate`:

```
Total: 1703.6 MB
1704.1 100.0% 100.0%   1704.1 100.0% __rust_alloc_zeroed (inline)
   0.0   0.0% 100.0%   1703.6 100.0% alloc::boxed::Box::new
   0.0   0.0% 100.0%   1703.6 100.0% crossbeam_epoch::atomic::Owned::new
   0.0   0.0% 100.0%   1703.6 100.0% metrics_util::registry::recency::Generational::with_increment
   0.0   0.0% 100.0%   1703.6 100.0% metrics_util::storage::bucket::AtomicBucket::push
   0.0   0.0% 100.0%   1703.6 100.0% reth_trie::trie::StateRoot::calculate
   0.0   0.0% 100.0%   1703.6 100.0% reth_optimism_trie::backfill::changesets::compute_trie_changesets_against_proofs
   0.0   0.0% 100.0%   1703.6 100.0% reth_optimism_trie::backfill::job::BackfillJob::compute_diff_with_snapshot_via
   0.0   0.0% 100.0%   1703.6 100.0% reth_optimism_trie::backfill::job::BackfillJob::backfill_block_with_snapshot
   0.0   0.0% 100.0%   1703.6 100.0% reth_optimism_trie::backfill::job::BackfillJob::run_with_snapshot
```

`metrics-util's` AtomicBucket is intentionally append-only (crossbeam-epoch-backed linked list of observations). The only way entries get released is by calling clear() / data(), which happens via the Prometheus render path when a metrics HTTP endpoint is scraped. The op-proofs CLI doesn't start a metrics endpoint, so the bucket is never drained.


**Steps to Reproduce**

1. Build with debug info preserved
2. Start a with jemalloc heap-profile dumps enabled
```
MALLOC_CONF="prof:true,prof_active:true,prof_prefix:/tmp/jeprof,lg_prof_sample:19,lg_prof_interval:34"
```
3. After backfill has been running for ~10 minutes, capture the baseline heap file
```
ls -t /tmp/jeprof.<pid>.*.heap | tail -3   # pick an early post-init dump
```
4. Wait 1–2 hours of backfill
5. Capture an endpoint heap file
```
ls -t /tmp/jeprof.<pid>.*.heap | head -1
```
6. Check the diff
```
jeprof --base=/tmp/jeprof.<pid>.<EARLY>.heap \
       --cum --text \
       /opt/op/optimism/rust/target/release/op-reth \
       /tmp/jeprof.<pid>.<LATE>.heap | head -30
```

Observe the call chain ending at `metrics_util::storage::bucket::AtomicBucket::push` accumulating proportional to elapsed wall-clock and blocks processed.

**Expected behavior**

- Anonymous memory should plateau after the initial allocator warm-up (typically within first ~30 min of any long-running operation).
- A backfill running for hours should not show monotonic memory growth tied to per-block work.

**Environment Information:**

Operating System: Ubuntu (Linux x86_64)
Chain: optimism (op-mainnet)
Backfill type: snapshot-accelerated (run_with_snapshot)
Backfill window: 1296000 blocks

**Configurations:**
```
op-reth proofs init \
  --chain=optimism \
  --datadir=/opt/op/data \
  --proofs-history.storage-path=/opt/op/proof-data-v2-with-backfill \
  --proofs-history.storage-version=v2
```

**Logs:**
NA

**Additional context**
NA

topPRs.title: fix(op-reth): report op-reth's own version instead of upstream reth's
topPRs.author: joshklop
topPRs.body:
## Summary
- `web3_clientVersion`, `engine_getClientVersionV1`, the CLI `--version` output, and the p2p `Hello` handshake identity all read a global singleton in `reth-node-core` that defaults to the pinned upstream `reth` crate's own version/commit. op-reth never overrode it, so all of these reported reth's version instead of op-reth's.
- Add a `build.rs` to the `op-reth` binary crate that emits op-reth-specific version/commit env vars (mirroring `reth-node-core`'s own `build.rs`, and `op-rbuilder`'s existing adaptation of it), and initialize the singleton with them via `try_init_version_metadata()` before the CLI is parsed.

## Test plan
- [x] `cargo build -p op-reth --bin op-reth` and confirmed `op-reth --version` now reports op-reth's own version + the monorepo's commit SHA instead of upstream reth's.
- [x] Ran `op-reth node --dev` locally and confirmed `web3_clientVersion` returns `op-reth/v<version>-<sha>/<target>` instead of `reth/v...`.
- [x] `cargo clippy -p op-reth --bin op-reth -- -D warnings` and `cargo +nightly fmt -p op-reth --check` are clean.

topPRs.title: ci: validate CircleCI schedule triggers
topPRs.author: ajsutton
topPRs.body:
Adds a CircleCI schedule-trigger validation script and wires it into CI where schedule wiring can drift.

The Bun script uses the repo-pinned `yq` to read CircleCI YAML, checks that scheduled continuation workflows are reachable from the setup decision tree, then queries the CircleCI schedule API with retry and verifies the configured schedule names exist. The check runs as a non-blocking `circleci-schedule-trigger-check` workflow on PRs that touch `.circleci/`, and on the `build_daily` scheduled pipeline so trigger drift is caught after external schedule changes.

Validation:
- `mise exec -- bun build .circleci/scripts/test-schedule-triggers.js --outfile=/tmp/test-schedule-triggers.js`
- `mise exec -- shellcheck .circleci/scripts/test-decision-tree.sh`
- `mise exec -- bash .circleci/scripts/test-decision-tree.sh`
- `mise exec -- bash .circleci/scripts/merge-configs.sh`
- `mise exec -- bash .circleci/scripts/test-continuation-params.sh /tmp/merged-config.yml`
- `mise exec -- semgrep scan --timeout=100 --config .semgrep/rules/ --error .`
- live local run of `bun .circleci/scripts/test-schedule-triggers.js` with `CIRCLE_API_TOKEN` set

topPRs.title: contracts-bedrock: handle disabled cannon fork state
topPRs.author: ajsutton
topPRs.body:
Updates the contracts fork test harness for post-U19 live network state.

U19 disables the legacy CANNON permissionless game on OP/Ink and leaves CANNON_KONA as the respected live game. The fork setup was still reading DelayedWETH and upgrade init bonds from CANNON, so fork upgrade tests could fail shared setup with invalid game configs.

This changes the harness to select the live permissionless game from AnchorStateRegistry first, fall back across known permissionless game types, and use a default nonzero permissionless init bond when simulating upgrade configs for a game type that is disabled on the live fork.

Validation:
- `mise exec -- forge build`
- `mise exec -- just build-go-ffi`
- `mise exec -- forge test --match-path test/L1/opcm/OPContractsManagerV2.t.sol --match-contract OPContractsManagerV2_Upgrade_Test` (skips without `FORK_TEST`)

Full live-network `just test-upgrade` validation is left to CI because no local `ETH_RPC_URL` archive RPC is configured in this shell.

topPRs.title: fix(op-reth/chainspec): derive bedrockBlock and regolithTime from config
topPRs.author: jyellick
topPRs.body:
## Summary

`to_genesis_chain_config` in the superchain-registry-driven chainspec path special-cases OP Mainnet (chain ID 10): `bedrock_block` is hardcoded to `Some(105235063)` for OP Mainnet and `Some(0)` for every other chain. Every other migrated chain currently in the bundled registry — Boba mainnet (`genesis.l2.number = 1149019`), Boba sepolia (`511`), and Celo mainnet (`31056500`) — therefore gets `bedrockBlock: 0`. Because `--rollup.historicalrpc` decides whether to forward an RPC request based on whether the block number is below `bedrockBlock`, those migrated chains silently never forward pre-bedrock requests — the flag is effectively a no-op.

`regolith_time` was likewise hardcoded to `Some(0)`, with no way for a chain config to express a non-zero value.

## Changes

This change removes the OP-Mainnet-specific special case for `bedrock_block` in favor of reading the value generically from each chain's config. It also unhardcodes `regolith_time`.

In `crates/chainspec/src/superchain/chain_metadata.rs`:

- Add `genesis.l2.number` to the `ChainMetadata` deserialization (introducing `GenesisMetadata` / `L2GenesisAnchor` helper structs).
- Read `bedrock_block` from `chain_config.genesis.l2.number` instead of hardcoding for OP Mainnet only. This is already the canonical bedrock activation block in every superchain-registry config: 0 for born-bedrock chains (Base, OP Sepolia, etc.), the migration block for migrated ones (OP Mainnet, Boba, Celo).
- Add `regolith_time` to `HardforkConfig` and read from `chain_config.hardforks.regolith_time`, defaulting to 0 when absent. No current chain in the bundled registry sets a non-zero value, so existing behavior is preserved.

The remaining OP-Mainnet-specific special case for the L1-style hardforks (`berlin_block` = 3950000, `london_block` / `arrow_glacier_block` / `gray_glacier_block` / `merge_netsplit_block` = 105235063) is intentionally untouched — those values are specific to OP Mainnet's OVM history and aren't carried in the registry. They could be derived too, but that's a separate change.

## Validation

Add a regression test using Celo mainnet (chain 42220) to exercise the non-OP-Mainnet migrated path. The existing OP Mainnet test now also exercises the new `genesis.l2.number`-driven code path, confirming the value `105235063` still emerges correctly.

```
$ cargo test -p reth-optimism-chainspec --features superchain-configs --lib superchain::
...
test superchain::chain_metadata::tests::test_convert_to_genesis_chain_config_migrated_non_op_mainnet ... ok
test superchain::chain_metadata::tests::test_convert_to_genesis_chain_config_op ... ok
test superchain::chain_metadata::tests::test_convert_to_genesis_chain_config ... ok
...
test result: ok. 13 passed; 0 failed
```

topPRs.title: contracts-bedrock: post-U19 cannon deprecation follow-ups
topPRs.author: mds1
topPRs.body:
Follow-ups to #21621, which handled the U19 fork state where the legacy `CANNON` permissionless game is disabled and `CANNON_KONA` is the live game.

Three changes:
1. Remove the transitional `CANNON`->`CANNON_KONA` `startingRespectedGameType` override from the fork test setup and the mirrored helpers in the OPCM V2 upgrade tests, now that `CANNON` is deprecated. Also drops the dead `_isPermissionlessGameType` helper.
2. Fix `FetchChainInfo` (op-fetcher), which derived the permissionless game only from `GameTypes.CANNON` and so reported no permissionless game for post-U19 chains. It now falls back to `CANNON_KONA` when `CANNON` is absent.
3. Pin the fork test block daily instead of weekly, so fork tests track live mainnet within a day rather than up to a week.

Unichain has run U19, but its upgrade landed after today's 00:00 UTC pinned block, so the `unichain-mainnet` fork job stays red until the daily pin rolls forward (2026-07-07). Verified green at a post-U19 block locally (29/29 in `OPContractsManagerV2_Upgrade_Test`). Everything else is green.

`FetchChainInfo` keeps its `CANNON` and `L2OutputOracle` handling on purpose, since op-fetcher syncs the whole superchain registry, which still has pre-U19 chains (`CANNON`) and legacy L2OO chains (e.g. fraxtal, race).

Follow-up: `MigrationValidationInput.cannonPrestate` is now dead, but removing it is a public ABI change so I'll do it separately.
